job.title: Marketing Manager
job.description:
MARKETING MANAGER, AUDIENCE GROWTH

Owned Channels & Messaging | Tempe, AZ (Hybrid)

THE ROLE

The organization is shifting from marketing its products to marketing to its audiences — the professionals it serves at every stage of their career, and the organizations that employ them. This role is how that shift gets executed.

You will own an assigned audience segment and the products that serve it. You take our annual strategy and turn it into a real plan — a message platform, a campaign calendar, a channel mix, and numbers you are accountable for — and then you build and run it. You are the person who writes the creative brief, decides what the email says, argues about the headline, and reads the report on Monday to find out whether you were right.

Your primary levers are our owned channels: email, website, organic social, search and lifecycle nurture. Our paid media is executed by an agency — you direct it, you don’t run it.

This is a hands-on manager role reporting to the Senior Marketing Manager. You will not manage people. You will manage plans, channels, agencies and outcomes.

WHAT YOU WILL OWN

Translate strategy into an executable plan.

Take annual goals and segment strategy and build the marketing plan for your audience: objectives, message platform, campaign calendar, channel mix, budget and success metrics. Bring it forward, defend it, and revise it quarterly against performance.

Run the organic engine.

Email, website content, SEO, organic social and nurture are your core channels. You own the calendar, the copy, the audience segmentation, the testing plan and the results.

Build it in HubSpot yourself.

You are proficient in HubSpot and work in it daily — building campaigns, emails, landing pages, forms, lists and segmented sequences, setting up workflows and nurture logic, and pulling your own reporting. You know how our data is structured, you keep it clean, and you can tell us what the platform is and isn’t telling us.

Develop messaging that resonates.

Build the message platform for your segment — what we say, to whom, and why they should care — grounded in persona research, competitive context and the language customers use. Translate product features into audience outcomes. If our marketing still reads like a product catalog, that is yours to fix.

Write the creative brief.

Produce briefs clear enough that internal designers, writers and outside agencies can execute without a second meeting. Review work against the brief. Send it back when it misses.

Direct paid, don’t execute it.

Define the audience, objective, offer, message and asset requirements for paid campaigns. Review performance with our agency and make the recommendation on where the next dollar goes.

Measure and adjust.

Build and track your campaigns in HubSpot, report results in plain language and change the plan when the data says to.

Work across the organization.

Partner with Product, Content, Publications, Education, Corporate Services and Membership. Much of this job is earning alignment from people who do not report to you.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN YEAR ONE

  • Your segment has a written, current marketing plan tied to revenue and audience goals — and your peers can describe it back to you.
  • Audience growth and engagement in your segment improve against a measured baseline: list growth, engaged contacts, content consumption, event and program participation.
  • The product lines in your portfolio hit their revenue targets, with clear line-of-sight from campaign to result.
  • Our messaging to your audience is consistent across email, web, social and paid — and reads like it was written for a person, not a product line.
  • Briefs go out complete, and creative comes back usable the first time.
  • You bring recommendations, not open questions, to your one-on-ones.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

These are requirements, not preferences.

  • 7+ years in marketing with direct ownership of campaigns carrying revenue or audience-growth targets. Product marketing, lifecycle marketing, segment marketing or integrated campaign backgrounds all fit.
  • Demonstrated ability to take a high-level strategy and produce a plan someone else could execute. We will ask you to walk us through one you built and what it delivered.
  • Strong writing. You will write subject lines, landing pages, ad copy, nurture sequences and briefs. Come prepared with samples; expect a writing exercise.
  • Hands-on ownership of owned channels — email marketing, website content, organic social and working SEO fundamentals.
  • Working proficiency in HubSpot or a comparable marketing automation platform. You build your own campaigns, lists, workflows, landing pages and reports — you do not submit requests for them.
  • Enough fluency in LinkedIn, Google and Microsoft ad platforms to brief an agency, read a performance report critically, and recognize when you are being sold something.
  • Fluent, daily use of AI tools for research, drafting, analysis and creative production. This is how our team works, not a bonus skill.
  • Ability to read campaign and audience data, explain what it means, and say what you would change.
  • Experience managing a marketing budget and making trade-off decisions inside it.
  • Proven cross-functional influence without formal authority.

A PLUS

  • Marketing experience in education, certification, membership or events.
  • Familiarity with procurement, supply chain, or a comparable professional community.
  • Association or mission-driven organization experience.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Marketing or a related field.

ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION

The organization has served its professional community for more than 110 years. It is a not-for-profit whose mission is to connect and empower the global professional community to advance individual and organizational success.

The organization operates on a hybrid model and currently requires employees to work in the office on Thursdays. The marketing team is small, which means your work is visible, your decisions are yours, and there is very little distance between an idea and its launch.

  • Experience characterizing igneous and metamorphic geologic environments is advantageous.

  • Must have strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Must be able to read, write and speak English at a level which will permit the employee to accurately understand and communicate information to safely and efficiently perform the job duties.

  • Must demonstrate accuracy and thoroughness to ensure quality performance.

  • Must possess a valid driver's license with a driving record acceptable to the company's auto insurance carrier.


Physical Requirements

  • The ability to work in a power plant and wellfield near hot pipes, drilling rigs and heavy equipment
  • The ability to navigate and work in remote field locations and work outdoors in difficult weather conditions

job.description:
Director of Material Handling

Mesa, Arizona | Relocation Assistance Provided


Our client is a rapidly growing North American manufacturer of highly engineered systems for data centers and other mission-critical environments. The company is making a significant investment in its expanding Mesa, Arizona manufacturing campus, including a new, state-of-the-art facility built for high-velocity production.

As the operation scales across additional production lines and shifts, the facility will manufacture approximately $1 billion of product annually and move more than $800 million of inventory through the operation each year.


The Director of Material Handling will own how all of it moves.


This is not a traditional warehouse leadership role. The opportunity is to design, implement and lead the complete material-handling system required to support a pull-based, takt-time-driven manufacturing operation—from the moment material arrives at the dock through storage, sequencing and line-side delivery.


The Director will determine how material is received and put away; where and how it is stored; how high-, medium- and low-runner parts are positioned; how materials are picked, kitted and sequenced; what moves by forklift, cart, runner or other conveyance; how internal milk runs operate; how parts are containerized and presented at point of use; and how the entire system scales as production grows.


Key Responsibilities

  • Own material flow from receiving through put-away, storage, picking, sequencing, replenishment, line-side delivery and returns.
  • Build and maintain a complete Plan For Every Part (PFEP) governing storage, containerization, replenishment, routing, presentation and inventory strategy.
  • Design warehouse layout, storage strategy and material locations based on part size, velocity, consumption and production requirements.
  • Develop internal milk runs, material routes and conveyance strategies to support continuous-flow production.
  • Establish kitting, sequencing, containerization and point-of-use presentation for assembly operations.
  • Implement Lean, pull-based replenishment systems including kanban, min/max and other signal-driven methods.
  • Own receiving discipline, inventory accuracy, cycle counting, physical inventory and material traceability.
  • Establish material-readiness and clear-to-build processes and lead recovery when shortages or inventory issues threaten production.
  • Build and lead the material-handling organization required to support multiple production lines and shifts.
  • Establish KPIs and continuously improve material availability, labor productivity, inventory accuracy, travel, space utilization and overall flow.


Candidate Profile

The successful candidate has built and operated material-flow systems before and knows what good looks like in a high-velocity manufacturing environment. Ideal experience includes:

  • 10–15+ years of progressive leadership in material handling, material flow, manufacturing logistics, warehouse operations or materials management.
  • Experience designing and implementing material-flow systems—not simply managing an established warehouse.
  • Strong experience in continuous-flow, takt-time-driven, pull-based or Lean manufacturing environments.
  • Hands-on expertise with PFEP, kanban, kitting, sequencing, milk runs, line-side replenishment, containerization and point-of-use delivery.
  • Experience with warehouse layout, receiving, put-away, inventory control, cycle counting and physical inventory.
  • Leadership of sizable hourly teams and frontline managers/supervisors in a multi-shift operation.
  • Demonstrated ability to scale systems, processes and teams as manufacturing volumes increase.
  • Strong ERP/MRP and data capabilities.

Relevant backgrounds may include automotive, heavy equipment, electronics, aerospace, industrial products, high-volume consumer manufacturing or other sophisticated manufacturing environments with continuous material flow.


This is a highly visible, hands-on leadership opportunity for someone who wants to design the system, build the organization and own its execution as the operation scales.

Comprehensive benefits and relocation assistance are provided.

firms. We have established clear product market fit and are now executing the transition from 

early scale to growth stage, launching a next-generation product suite with significant expansion 

ahead.

everything that happens after a customer signs, and to build the discipline, structure, and 

strategic clarity that the next chapter demands. They have taken a tactical service and support 

organization stuck in a reactive motion and transformed it into a strategic, forward-thinking team 

that creates a competitive advantage.


What You’ll Own:

The post-sale operating system, end-to-end. You will lead a team of approximately 20 across Customer Success, Technical Support, and Relationship Management. The mandate is not to manage this organization; it is to transform it: from reactive and account-managed to proactive, data-driven, and commercially oriented. 


Core Responsibilities:


1. Client Retention and Revenue Protection: The right candidate will build the team and instill the culture to ensure the following are accomplished:

• Own Net Revenue Retention (NRR) as the leading operational metric. Identify at-risk accounts early, drive structured recovery playbooks, and hold the team accountable to outcomes rather than activity.

• Build the infrastructure for proactive client engagement: health scoring, early warning signals, escalation protocols, and executive-level relationship coverage on strategic accounts.

• Convert the Relationship Management function into a commercial driver, surfacing expansion opportunities and closing them rather than simply identifying them.


2. Customer Success and Support Transformation: We are looking for someone who has demonstrably transformed a service and support organization. Not optimized one, not inherited a good one, but taken a reactive, under-structured function and rebuilt it into something that retains clients, generates expansion revenue, and earns trust with sophisticated buyers.

• Lead the Customer Success and Support organization through a fundamental shift from a ticket closure culture to a value delivery culture.

• Define tiered service models appropriate to client size and complexity. Allocate Customer Service Managers (CSM) and Technical Account Managers (TAM) resources against accounts where investment will be recovered and make deliberate decisions about the rest.

• Build the playbooks, escalation paths, and accountability structures the team needs to operate with consistency and confidence.

• Establish executive relationship coverage for top-tier accounts and personally own several of the most strategic client relationships.


3. Operating Rhythm and Accountability:

• Establish and maintain the company’s operating cadence: weekly business reviews, 

cross-functional alignment, and clear accountability structures that translate PE 

mandated growth targets into departmental execution.

• Translate the CEO’s strategic priorities into department-level plans with named owners, 

timelines, and measurable outcomes.

• Maintain a lean, high-output organization. Build scale through improved efficiencies, 

processes, and tooling before adding headcount. All headcount additions must be justified 

by capacity modeling rather than urgency or noise.


4. Product Feedback Loop and Launch Readiness:

• Serve as the operational bridge between customer-facing teams and Product and Engineering. Customer insights must become product inputs in a structured, repeatable way rather than through ad hoc escalations.

• Own readiness for our upcoming product launch: training, documentation, support playbooks, and the client communication strategy.


5. PE Reporting and Board Level Visibility:

• Define, own, and report on the core operational KPIs: Churn, NRR, CSAT, Gross Margin on Services, Support Efficiency, and Time to Value.

• Partner with the CEO in preparing Board materials and reporting to Marlin Equity Partners. Understand what drives valuation in a PE context and operate accordingly.


6. Professional Services and Implementation (Scope Dependent)

For the right candidate, this role will also include oversight of the Professional Services and Implementation function. This is not a requirement of the role at the outset. It is an expansion of scope available to a candidate with demonstrated PS leadership experience and the bandwidth to absorb it without compromising the core Customer Success and retention mandate.



What We’re Looking For:


Non-negotiable:

• 10+ years of operational leadership in a B2B SaaS environment as a COO, VP of Customer Success, or VP of Operations with P&L exposure.

• Enterprise SaaS client experience. You have managed a team that supports a vertical solution with industry-specific workflows and analytics.

• A proven transformation track record. You have taken a service or support organization that was substandard, structurally, culturally, and commercially, and rebuilt it into a high performing team. You can point to the before, the after, and what you did to get there.

• PE environment fluency. You understand the pace, the reporting requirements, and the metrics that matter to a financial sponsor. You are comfortable being accountable to a Board.

• SaaS model expertise. Deep familiarity with churn economics, recurring revenue retention, NRR benchmarking, and the tradeoffs in Customer Success resource allocation.

• A builder’s orientation. This role requires constructing systems, not inheriting them. You are energized by a blank canvas and frustrated by stagnation.

• Denver-based. This team needs an on-site leader.


Preferred:

• Experience in financial technology, alternative asset management software, or adjacent capital markets infrastructure. Our clients are among the most sophisticated buyers in the market, and familiarity with how GPs operate is a genuine advantage.

• PS or Implementation leadership experience, for candidates interested in the expanded scope described above. 


Why This Role:

Our client is looking for a builder first and foremost — someone who thrives in the field, leads by doing, and possesses unmatched mechanical, fabrication, and installation skills. The Manager of Automated Gate


Installations will lead the division’s field operations, oversee installations from inception to completion, troubleshoot and resolve technical challenges, and elevate team performance, client satisfaction, and operational efficiency. Field Leadership & Execution

Team & Client Management

Strategic Growth & Development

Required Qualifications

  • Deep expertise in automated gate systems and access control installation and service.
  • Strong command of construction methodologies, field logistics, and equipment usage.
  • Proven experience managing field teams and project operations.
  • Excellent interpersonal, customer service, and team leadership skills.
  • High integrity, reliability, and passion for quality and craftsmanship.

·       Fabrication and installation experience of gates of all types and materials including steel, aluminum, wood, and AZEK. Welding experience with aluminum and stainless steel is also required.


Compensation & Benefits:

  • Competitive executive compensation package.
  • Full benefits include health, retirement, and paid time off.
  • Company vehicle, tools, and relocation assistance for the right candidate.
  • Career development opportunities and a leadership seat in a high-growth company.


Who You Are:

You’re not just a technical expert — you’re a builder, a leader, and a collaborator. You’re looking for your next big chapter at a company that values craftsmanship, ownership, and growth. You believe in fixing what’s broken, mentoring others, and delivering jaw-dropping results. If you're ready to lead a team, elevate a division, and help drive a company’s future, we want to talk to you.

job.description:
Summary

The primary function of the Loan Officer is to support & enhance the Branch Manager's book of business. (The Branch Manager generates new leads and brings in new contacts/prospects) Proactively originating real estate loans and generating loan leads from the Branch database of existing clients, on behalf of the Branch Manager. Interview applicants to assist with the completion of a thorough real estate application, provide assistance with the applicant's selection of the loan program that best meets his/her needs, and prequalify the applicants to determine credit worthiness.


Essential Job Functions

  • Provide exemplary service that meets and exceeds our customer's expectations. Ensure transactions are accurately and smoothly transitioned to the processing team.
  • Be registered/licensed with the Nationwide Mortgage Licensing System (NMLS) and Registry to comply with the S.A.F.E. Act.
  • Solicit real estate loans in accordance with agency standards and loan production goals by calling prospective referral sources and clients from the Branch Manager’s pending pipeline.
  • Enhance & maintain relationships with realtors, brokers, home builders, and other referral sources to ensure continued growth and referral business.
  • Maintain & manage an active calling program for solicitation purposes, through the use of Annual Review calls and pending pipeline calls, as dictated by SPEAR.
  • Price out different options and provide multiple loan scenarios to prospective clients, using Mortgage Coach and SPEAR.
  • Explain and communicate terms, provide guidance and information relevant to the risks and benefit of each loan program, and set realistic expectations for borrowers.
  • Analyze loan applications to ensure FNMA, FHLMC, FHA, VA, Correspondent, Broker and Warehouse guidelines are met. Thoroughly analyze the borrower's credit history and determine credit worthiness. Responsibilities also include recognition of suspicious or fraudulent activities.
  • Remain the front line contact with customers to ensure outstanding customer service. Follows up with realtor and borrower to update loan status and answer any questions; to include any significant changes regarding loan processing, approval loan terms, closing dates and Final HUD review.
  • Complies with applicable mortgage laws and policies; ensures compliance with HMDA requirements.
  • Provides interest rates, products and services information to customers throughout the loan process. Responsible for locking rates and restructuring loans if needed.
  • Attend weekly sales meeting to discuss workflow, efficiencies, address any pertinent issues of concern, allowing employees to ask questions of new product information and procedures, general corporate information, etc.
  • Perform any duties/activities assigned by management


Qualifications

  • Bachelor Degree in Business, Finance, Marketing or related field or equivalent work experience.
  • 2+ year’s real estate, mortgage origination or related experience.
  • Must be proficient with RESPA/TIL, Federal, State and regulatory procedures and practices. Knowledge of processing, closing, underwriting and all other aspects of the mortgage loan process.
  • Must be familiar with PMI, Fannie, Freddie, FHA, and VA guidelines, including how those affect automated Underwriting Systems - DU/LP.
  • Strong communication, oral, organizational, analytical, problem solving and time management skills; ability to work in stressful situations
  • Knowledge of computers and basic computer skills.
